bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷三十四 一行傳第二十二: 鄭遨 石昂 程福贇 李自倫
title.en: Volume 34 Biographies of Recluses 14: Zhen Gao, Shi Ang, Cheng Fuyun, Li Zilun
title.raw: 卷三十四 一行傳第二十二: 鄭遨 石昂 程福贇 李自倫 Volume 34 Biographies of Recluses 14: Zhen Gao, Shi Ang, Cheng Fuyun, Li Zilun

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，五代之亂極矣，《傳》所謂「天地閉，賢人隱」之時歟！

translations.literal: Alas, the disorder of the Five Dynasties reached its extreme—is this not the time the “Records” calls “Heaven and Earth shut, worthy men in hiding”?
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the Five Dynasties’ chaos reached its height. Was this not the age the Records call “Heaven and Earth shut, worthy men in hiding”?

sentences.zh: 當此之時，臣弒其君，子弒其父，而搢紳之士安其祿而立其朝，充然無復廉恥之色者皆是也。

translations.literal: In that age ministers murdered their lords and sons murdered their fathers, while gentry and officials took their salaries and stood in court, all replete and without the color of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers murdered lords, sons murdered fathers, yet officials took salary and stood in court without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 吾以謂自古忠臣義士多出於亂世，而怪當時可道者何少也，豈果無其人哉？

translations.literal: I hold that loyal ministers and righteous men have always come forth in ages of disorder—yet I marvel that so few in that time were worth speaking of; was it truly that there were no such men?
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers and righteous men usually rise in chaotic ages—yet how few in that time were worth naming. Were there truly none?

sentences.zh: 雖曰干戈興，學校廢，而禮義衰，風俗隳壞，至於如此，然自古天下未嘗無人也，吾意必有潔身自負之士，嫉世遠去而不可見者。

translations.literal: Though it is said arms were raised, schools abandoned, ritual and righteousness declined, and custom ruined to such a point—yet the world has never been without men; I believe there were men of clean conduct who scorned the age, went far off, and could not be seen.
translations.idiomatic: War rose, schools fell, ritual decayed, custom collapsed—yet the world has never lacked men. Surely some of clean conduct scorned the age and withdrew beyond sight.

sentences.zh: 自古材賢有韞於中而不見於外，或窮居陋巷，委身草莽，雖顏子之行，不遇仲尼而名不彰，況世變多故，而君子道消之時乎！

translations.literal: From antiquity talent and worth have been stored within and not shown without, or dwelt in poor lanes and cast themselves on the wild—though Yan Hui’s conduct, without meeting Confucius, would not have won fame; how much more in an age of many changes when the gentleman’s Way was in decline!
translations.idiomatic: Talent often hides within and never shows without—men in poor lanes, lost in the wild. Even Yan Hui’s virtue needed Confucius to be known; how much more when the gentleman’s Way was fading in constant turmoil!

sentences.zh: 吾又以謂必有負材能，修節義，而沈淪於下，泯沒而無聞者。

translations.literal: I also hold that there were men of talent and ability who cultivated integrity and righteousness yet sank below and were drowned without a hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Surely too were men of talent and integrity who sank below and died unheard.

sentences.zh: 求之傳記，而亂世崩離，文字殘缺，不可復得，然僅得者四五人而已。

translations.literal: Seeking in records, in disorder and collapse the writing is broken and cannot be recovered; yet of those barely found there are only four or five.
translations.idiomatic: Records of that collapse are broken; little can be recovered. I find only four or five men.

sentences.zh: 處乎山林而群麋鹿，雖不足以為中道，然與其食人之祿，俯首而包羞，孰若無愧於心，放身而自得，吾得二人焉，曰鄭遨、張薦明。

translations.literal: Dwelling in mountains and forests among herds of deer—though not enough for the Mean—yet compared with eating another’s salary, bowing the head and wrapping shame, which is better than a heart without guilt, letting the body go free and finding ease? I find two such men: Zheng Ao and Zhang Jianming.
translations.idiomatic: Living among deer in the hills is not the Mean—but better than eating another’s salary, bowing in shame. I find two such men: Zheng Ao and Zhang Jianming.

sentences.zh: 勢利不屈其心，去就不違其義，吾得一人焉，曰石昂。

translations.literal: Profit and power did not bend his heart; leaving or staying did not violate his righteousness—I find one such man: Shi Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Profit and power never bent him; leaving or staying never broke his code—I find one: Shi Ang.

sentences.zh: 茍利於君，以忠獲罪，而何必自明，有至死而不言者，此古之義士也，吾得一人焉，曰程福赟。

translations.literal: If it profited the lord, to be punished for loyalty—why must one clear oneself? There are those who to death never speak—such are the righteous men of old; I find one such man: Cheng Fuyun.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the lord brought punishment for loyalty—yet he never cleared himself, dying silent: an ancient righteous man. I find one: Cheng Fuyun.

sentences.zh: 五代之亂，君不君，臣不臣，父不父，子不子，至於兄弟、夫婦人倫之際，無不大壞，而天理幾乎其滅矣。

translations.literal: In the disorder of the Five Dynasties, lord was not lord, minister not minister, father not father, son not son—even between brothers and in the relations of husband and wife human bonds were utterly broken, and Heaven’s principle was nearly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties’ chaos, lord, minister, father, son—all bonds broke; even between brothers and spouses human ties collapsed, and Heaven’s principle nearly died.

sentences.zh: 於此之時，能以孝悌自修於一鄉，而風行於天下者，猶或有之，然其事跡不著，而無可紀次，獨其名氏或因見於書者，吾亦不敢沒，而其略可錄者，吾得一人焉，曰李自倫。

translations.literal: Even then, men who by filial piety and brotherly duty cultivated themselves in one village and whose wind spread through the realm may still have existed—but their deeds are not prominent and cannot be arranged in order; only their names perhaps appear in writing—I dare not omit them; of what can briefly be recorded I find one man: Li Zilun.
translations.idiomatic: Some may still have practiced filial piety in one village until the realm felt it—but their deeds are thin, their names only scattered in documents. Of what can be sketched I find one: Li Zilun.

sentences.zh: 作《一行傳》。

translations.literal: I composed the “Biographies of Recluses.”
translations.idiomatic: Hence I wrote the “Biographies of Recluses.”

sentences.zh: 鄭遨

translations.literal: Zheng Ao
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ao

sentences.zh: （張薦明附）〉

translations.literal: (Zhang Jianming appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zhang Jianming appended)〉

sentences.zh: 鄭遨，字雲叟，滑州白馬人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Ao, courtesy name Yunsong, was a man of Baima in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ao, courtesy name Yunsong, was from Baima in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗祖廟諱遨，故世行其字。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong of Tang’s ancestral temple tabooed the character ao, so the world used his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong’s ancestral taboo forbade the character ao, so the world used his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 遨少好學，敏於文辭。

translations.literal: Ao in youth loved study and was quick at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning and wrote with ease.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗時，舉進士不中，見天下已亂，有拂衣遠去之意，欲攜其妻、子與俱隱，其妻不從，遨及入少室山為道士。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he entered the jinshi examinations and failed; seeing the realm already in disorder, he had the will to shake off his robes and go far off, wishing to take wife and children into hiding together—his wife would not follow; Ao thereupon entered Mount Shaoshi as a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhaozong he failed the jinshi; seeing chaos, he wished to flee with wife and children—his wife refused; he entered Mount Shaoshi as a Daoist.

sentences.zh: 其妻數以書勸遨還家，輒投之於火，後聞其妻、子卒，一慟而止。

translations.literal: His wife several times wrote urging Ao to return home; he always threw the letters into the fire; later hearing his wife and children had died, he mourned once and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His wife wrote again and again; he burned each letter; when he heard she and the children were dead, he grieved once and stopped.

sentences.zh: 遨與李振故善，振後事梁貴顯，欲以祿遨，遨不顧，後振得罪南竄，遨徒步千里往省之，由是聞者益高其行。

translations.literal: Ao had been friendly with Li Zhen; Zhen later served Liang in high honor and wished to give Ao an office—Ao paid no heed; later Zhen was punished and fled south; Ao walked a thousand li on foot to visit him, and hearers all the more exalted his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He had been close to Li Zhen; when Zhen rose high in Liang and offered him office, Ao refused; when Zhen was disgraced and fled south, Ao walked a thousand li to see him—and his fame grew.

sentences.zh: 其後，遨聞華山有五粒松，脂淪入地，千歲化為藥，能去三屍，因徙居華陰，欲求之。

translations.literal: Later Ao heard that on Mount Hua there were five-kernel pines whose resin sank into the earth and after a thousand years became medicine that could expel the three corpses; he moved to Huayin to seek it.
translations.idiomatic: He heard Mount Hua’s five-kernel pines oozed resin that, buried a thousand years, became medicine to expel the three corpses; he moved to Huayin to seek it.

sentences.zh: 與道士李道殷、羅隱之友善，世目以為三高士。

translations.literal: He was friendly with the Daoist Li Daoyin and Luo Yin; the age called them the Three High Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended the Daoist Li Daoyin and Luo Yin; the age called them the Three High Recluses.

sentences.zh: 遨種田，隱之賣藥以自給，道殷有釣魚術，鉤而不餌，又能化石為金，遨嘗驗其信然，而不之求也。

translations.literal: Ao farmed; Yin sold medicine to support themselves; Daoyin had an art of fishing—hook without bait—and could also turn stone to gold; Ao once tested him and found it true, yet did not ask for it.
translations.idiomatic: Ao farmed; Yin sold herbs; Daoyin fished with hook but no bait and could turn stone to gold—Ao proved it true yet never asked.

sentences.zh: 節度使劉遂凝數以寶貨遺之，遨一不受。

translations.literal: Military governor Liu Suining several times sent him treasures; Ao never accepted one.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Suining sent treasures repeatedly; Ao refused every gift.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗時以左拾遺、晉高祖時以諫議大夫召之，皆不起，即賜號為逍遙先生。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong of Tang he was summoned as Left Reminder; under Gaozu of Jin as Censor; he rose for neither; they at once granted him the title Master Free Wanderer.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong summoned him as Left Reminder, Gaozu as Censor—he refused both and was named Master Free Wanderer.

sentences.zh: 天福四年卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianfu he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth Tianfu year, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 遨之節高矣，遭亂世不汙於榮利，至棄妻、子不顧而去，豈非與世自絕而篤愛其身者歟？

translations.literal: Ao’s integrity was high; in a disorderly age he was not stained by glory and profit—even abandoning wife and children without regard and going away—is this not cutting oneself off from the world and loving one’s person deeply?
translations.idiomatic: Ao’s integrity was high; in chaos he scorned rank and gain—even abandoning wife and children. Did he not cut himself off from the world to keep himself whole?

sentences.zh: 然遨好飲酒弈棋，時時為詩章落人間，人間多寫以縑素，相贈遺以為寶，至或圖寫其形，玩於屋壁，其跡雖遠而其名愈彰，與乎石門、荷之徒異矣。

translations.literal: Yet Ao loved wine and weiqi, and from time to time let poems fall into the world; people often copied them on silk and gave them as treasures, even painting his likeness to hang on walls; though his tracks were far, his name grew the more renowned—different from men like those of Shimen and He.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved wine and chess, and poems reached the world; people copied them on silk as treasures and painted him on walls—far in the hills, yet more famous than recluses like those of Shimen and He.

sentences.zh: 與遨同時張薦明者，燕人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianming of the same time was a man of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporary Zhang Jianming was from Yan.

sentences.zh: 少以儒學遊河朔，後去為道士，通老子、莊周之說。

translations.literal: In youth he traveled the Hebei region as a Confucian scholar; later he left that and became a Daoist, penetrating the teachings of Laozi and Zhuang Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Young he studied Confucianism in Hebei; later he became a Daoist versed in Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 高祖召見，問「道家可以治國乎？

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned him and asked, “Can the Daoist teaching govern the state?”
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned him and asked, “Can Daoism govern the state?”

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「道也者，妙萬物而為言，得其極者，屍居衽席之間可以治天地也。

translations.literal: He replied: “The Dao is that which subtly accounts for the ten thousand things in speech; one who attains its utmost can govern Heaven and Earth while the corpse lies between mat and coverlet.”
translations.idiomatic: He replied, “The Dao accounts for all things in speech; at its utmost one governs Heaven and Earth while lying between mat and coverlet.”

sentences.zh: 」高祖大其言，延入內殿講《道德經》，拜以為師。

translations.literal: Gaozu magnified his words, drew him into the inner hall to lecture on the “Classic of the Way and Its Power,” and honored him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu prized his words, drew him into the inner hall to lecture on the Daodejing, and honored him as teacher.

sentences.zh: 薦明聞宮中奉時鼓，曰：「陛下聞鼓乎？

translations.literal: Jianming heard the palace observe the seasonal drum and said, “Your Majesty hears the drum?”
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the palace drum for the seasons, Jianming said, “Does Your Majesty hear the drum?”

sentences.zh: 其聲一而已。

translations.literal: Its sound is one only.
translations.idiomatic: Its sound is one.

sentences.zh: 五音十二律，鼓無一焉，然和之者鼓也。

translations.literal: Among the five tones and twelve pitch pipes the drum has not one—yet what harmonizes them is the drum.
translations.idiomatic: Of five tones and twelve pipes the drum holds not one—yet harmony depends on the drum.

sentences.zh: 夫一，萬事之本也，能守一者可以治天下。

translations.literal: The One is the root of the ten thousand affairs; one who can keep the One can govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The One is the root of all things; whoever keeps the One can govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 」高祖善之，賜號通玄先生，後不知其所終。

translations.literal: Gaozu approved and granted him the title Master Penetrating Mystery; later his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu approved and named him Master Penetrating Mystery; later his end is unknown.

sentences.zh: 石昂，青州臨淄人也。

translations.literal: Shi Ang was a man of Linzi in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ang was from Linzi in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 家有書數千卷，喜延四方之士，士無遠近，多就昂學問，食其門下者或累歲，昂未嘗有怠色。

translations.literal: His household had several thousand volumes; he delighted in gathering scholars from all quarters; whether near or far, many came to Ang for learning; some ate at his gate for years—Ang never showed weariness.
translations.idiomatic: His house held thousands of books; scholars came from far and near; some stayed years at his gate—he never showed weariness.

sentences.zh: 而昂不求仕進。

translations.literal: Yet Ang did not seek office.
translations.idiomatic: He never sought office.

sentences.zh: 節度使符習高基行，召以為臨淄令。

translations.literal: Military governor Fu Xi, admiring his conduct, summoned him and made him magistrate of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fu Xi, admiring his conduct, made him magistrate of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 習入朝京師，監軍楊彥朗知留後事，昂以公事至府上謁，贊者以彥朗諱「石」，更其姓曰「右」。

translations.literal: When Xi entered the capital, Supervisory Army officer Yang Yanlang held affairs as regent; Ang came to the prefecture on public business to pay respects; the usher, because Yanlang tabooed the character “stone,” changed his surname to “right.”
translations.idiomatic: Xi went to court; Yang Yanlang held the command as regent; Ang came on public business; the usher, because Yanlang tabooed “stone,” changed his surname to “right.”

sentences.zh: 昂趨於庭，仰責彥朗曰：「內侍奈何以私害公！

translations.literal: Ang hurried into the court, looked up, and reproached Yanlang: “How can an inner attendant harm the public with private spite!”
translations.idiomatic: Ang strode into court and rebuked Yanlang: “How can a eunuch harm the public for private spite!”

sentences.zh: 昂姓『石』，非『右』也。

translations.literal: My surname is “Shi,” not “Right.”
translations.idiomatic: My surname is Shi, not Right.

sentences.zh: 」彥朗大怒，拂衣起去，昂即趨出。

translations.literal: Yanlang in great rage flung his robes and rose; Ang at once hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang in rage swept out; Ang fled at once.

sentences.zh: 解官還於家，語其子曰：「吾本不欲仕亂世，果為刑人所辱，子孫其以我為戒！」

translations.literal: He resigned his post and returned home, telling his sons: “I never wished to serve a disorderly age—yet I have been shamed by a criminal; let my descendants take me as a warning!”
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and told his sons, “I never wished to serve chaos—yet a criminal shamed me; take me as your warning!”

sentences.zh: 昂父亦好學，平生不喜拂說，父死，昂於柩前誦《尚書》，曰：「此吾先人之所欲聞也。

translations.literal: Ang’s father also loved study and in life disliked flattery; when the father died, Ang before the bier recited the “Documents,” saying: “This is what my forebear wished to hear.”
translations.idiomatic: His father too loved learning and hated flattery; at the bier Ang recited the Documents: “This is what my father wished to hear.”

sentences.zh: 」禁其家不可以佛事汙吾先人。

translations.literal: He forbade his household to defile the forebear with Buddhist rites.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade Buddhist rites that would defile his father.

sentences.zh: 程福赟

translations.literal: Cheng Fuyun
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Fuyun

sentences.zh: 程福赟者，不知其世家。

translations.literal: Cheng Fuyun—his lineage is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Fuyun’s lineage is unknown.

sentences.zh: 為人沈厚寡言而有勇。

translations.literal: As a man he was deep, sparing of words, and brave.
translations.idiomatic: He was deep, quiet, and brave.

sentences.zh: 少為軍卒，以戰功累遷洺州團練使。

translations.literal: In youth he was a common soldier; by battle merit he rose step by step to regent of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a common soldier and rose by battle merit to regent of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 晉出帝時，為奉國右廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Chu of Jin he was commander of the Fengguo right wing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chu of Jin he commanded the Fengguo right wing.

sentences.zh: 開運中，契丹入寇，出帝北征，奉國軍士乘間夜縱火焚營，欲因以為亂，福赟身自救火被傷，火滅而亂者不得發。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era the Khitans invaded; Emperor Chu marched north; Fengguo troops seized the interval of night to set fire to the camp, intending to make disorder; Fuyun himself ran to fight the fire and was wounded; when the fire was out the plotters could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyun era, with Chu marching north against the Khitans, Fengguo troops set the camp ablaze by night to mutiny; Fuyun fought the fire himself, was wounded, and quelled the plot.

sentences.zh: 福赟以為契丹且大至，而天子在軍，京師虛空，不宜以小故動搖人聽，因匿其事不以聞。

translations.literal: Fuyun thought the Khitans would soon come in force while the Son of Heaven was with the army and the capital empty—a small matter should not shake men’s hearts; he therefore hid the affair and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: He believed the Khitans would come in force while the emperor was in the field and the capital empty—a small fire should not panic the army; he hid the affair and did not report it.

sentences.zh: 軍將李殷位次福赟下，利其去而代之，因誣福赟與亂者同謀，不然何以不奏。

translations.literal: The army officer Li Yin ranked below Fuyun, coveted his place, and slandered him, saying Fuyun was of one plot with the mutineers—otherwise why not memorialize?
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin, junior to him, coveted his post and accused him of joining the mutineers—otherwise why hide it from court?

sentences.zh: 出帝下福赟獄，人皆以為冤，福赟終不自辨以見殺。

translations.literal: Emperor Chu put Fuyun in prison; all held it unjust; Fuyun to the end would not clear himself and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chu imprisoned him; all called it unjust; Fuyun never defended himself and was executed.

sentences.zh: 李自倫

translations.literal: Li Zilun
translations.idiomatic: Li Zilun

sentences.zh: 李自倫者，深州人也。

translations.literal: Li Zilun was a man of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zilun was from Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 天福四年正月，尚書戶部奏：「深州司功參軍李自倫六世同居，奉敕準格。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Tianfu the Ministry of Revenue memorialized: “Li Zilun, Assistant in the Ministry of Revenue of Shenzhou, six generations dwelling together—per imperial order and statute.”
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu’s fourth year, first month, the Ministry of Revenue reported: “Li Zilun of Shenzhou, six generations under one roof—per statute and edict.”

sentences.zh: 按格，孝義旌表，必先加按驗，孝者復其終身，義門仍加旌表。

translations.literal: According to the statute, to honor filial piety one must first add investigation and verification; the filial are restored for life, and gates of righteousness receive further commendation.
translations.idiomatic: By statute, filial piety must be verified first; the filial are exempt for life, and righteous households receive further honors.

sentences.zh: 得本州審到鄉老程言等稱，自倫高祖訓，訓生粲，粲生則，則生忠，忠生自倫，自倫生光厚，六世同居不妄。

translations.literal: The prefecture verified through village elders Cheng Yan and others, who said: from Zilun’s great-grandfather Xun, Xun begot Can, Can begot Ze, Ze begot Zhong, Zhong begot Zilun, Zilun begot Guanghou—six generations dwelling together without falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture verified through elders Cheng Yan and others: from great-grandfather Xun through Can, Ze, Zhong, Zilun, to Guanghou—six generations, no falsehood.

sentences.zh: 」敕以所居飛鳧鄉為孝義鄉，匡聖裏為仁和裏，準式旌表門閭。

translations.literal: An edict named their dwelling Feiniao Village as Village of Filial Piety, Kuangsheng Lane as Lane of Humaneness, and honored their gate by the prescribed form.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed their village Village of Filial Piety, their lane Lane of Humaneness, and honored their gate by statute.

sentences.zh: 九月丙子，戶部復奏：「前登州義門王仲昭六世同居，其旌表有聽事、步欄，前列屏，樹烏頭正門，閥閱一丈二尺，烏頭二柱端冒以瓦桶，築雙闕一丈，在烏頭之南三丈七尺，夾樹槐柳，十有五步，請如之。

translations.literal: On bingzi of the ninth month the Ministry memorialized again: “Formerly the righteous gate Wang Zhongzhao of Dengzhou, six generations dwelling together—their commendation had a hall, balustraded steps, a screen before the row, black-headed main gate, a meritorious record one zhang two chi, black-headed twin pillars capped with tile barrels, twin towers one zhang south of the black head at three zhang seven chi, locust and willow planted fifteen paces apart—we beg it be as this.”
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Ministry cited Wang Zhongzhao of Dengzhou, another six-generation household, whose gate had hall, screen, black-headed pillars, memorial tablet, twin towers, and planted trees—and asked that Zilun’s gate match.

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「此故事也，令式無之。

translations.literal: The edict said: “This is old precedent; the current code has it not.”
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, “That is old precedent; the current code has no such rule.”

sentences.zh: 其量地之宜，高其外門，門安綽楔，左右建臺，高一丈二尺，廣狹方正稱焉，圬以白而赤其四角，使不孝不義者見之，可以悛心而易行焉。」

translations.literal: Measure the ground as fit, raise the outer gate, set the door with a threshold block, build platforms left and right one zhang two chi high, square in breadth and depth as fitting, plaster white and redden the four corners, so that the unfilial and unrighteous seeing them may repent in heart and change their conduct.”
translations.idiomatic: “Measure the ground, raise the outer gate, set the threshold, build left and right platforms one zhang two chi high, plaster them white and redden the corners—so the unfilial and unrighteous may see and repent.”
